newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate ends down on heavy demand.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate ends down on heavy demand.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates closed down 110 basis points at 23.00 percent on Friday on heavy demand in late trade, dealers said.
"Buyers flooded the market at the close, that's why rates began to fall," a trader said.
Dealers put demand for paper down to a stable peso, lower yields on U.S. long bonds and signs the central bank intended to cap recent rises in secondary market rates.
Benchmark 48-hour peso contracts closed down 0.8 of a centavo at 7.8670/7.8695 per dollar.
U.S. 30-year Treasury bonds ended up 5/32 at 7.05 percent.
Banco de Mexico again offset surplus liquidity from the system, by draining 7.393 billion pesos through a combination of direct sales of government paper and repurchase agreements.
The central bank assigned the direct sales at rates of between 22.64-23.91 percent, and the repurchase agreements at between 22.11-22.80 percent.
Friday's assignment rates were considerably down from Tuesday, when they were assigned at levels as high as 28.70 percent.
Overnight rates on bank paper meanwhile ended down 250 basis points at 23.00 percent.
June contracts on the Chicago Cetes futures market closed up 45 centavos at 78.25 pesos.
Liquidity of 6.889 billion pesos was scheduled to return to the system on Monday from prior central bank participation, in addition to bills worth one billion pesos.
